subject: general
question: A gas can be liquefied by _________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**high pressure and low temperature**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Gases can be liquefied by increasing the **pressure** and decreasing the **temperature**.
 
• Increasing the **pressure** forces gas molecules closer together, promoting the formation of a liquid phase.
 
• Decreasing the **temperature** reduces the kinetic energy of the gas molecules, making it easier for intermolecular forces to hold the molecules together in a liquid state.
 
• These principles are based on the **Ideal Gas Law** and **Phase Diagrams** which describe the state of matter under different conditions of pressure and temperature.
 
• Liquefaction of gases is a fundamental process in the production and storage of **liquefied natural gas (LNG)**, **liquefied petroleum gas (LPG)**, and in the industrial gas industry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Low pressure and high temperature**__

 __
 
• Low pressure and high temperature conditions generally favor the formation of gases rather than liquids because the molecules have high kinetic energy and are far apart.
 
 
 
• **Low pressure and low temperature**__
 __
 
• While low temperature can support liquefaction, low pressure does not help in bringing molecules close together, making it ineffective for liquefying gases.
 
 
 
• **High pressure and high temperature**__
 
 
• High pressure can promote liquefaction, but high temperature increases the kinetic energy of molecules, counteracting the effects of high pressure.
